LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we write short notes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Explain the main ideas in Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information
2. Give Kenyan examples for Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information
3. Practise Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information at school and at home

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 3.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION
This lesson teaches Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information for Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. Explain the main ideas in Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. Give Kenyan examples for Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. Practise Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information at school and at home
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information above.
2. Explain Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write short notes?
2. How do you write short notes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Explain the main ideas in Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information
2. Give Kenyan examples for Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information
3. Practise Writing 3.3.1 Writing for Information at school and at home

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
